vocabulary.definition: Listing what divides a number evenly (its factors) and what it divides into evenly (its multiples), then finding what two numbers share.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Listar lo que divide un número exactamente (sus factores) y lo que el número forma al contar de esa cantidad (sus múltiplos), y luego hallar lo que dos números comparten.
vocabulary.visual: GCF of 48 and 36 is 12 · LCM of 6 and 8 is 24
vocabulary.cloze: Factors ___ a number; multiples are what it ___.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number that divides another number evenly, with no remainder.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero que divide a otro exactamente, sin residuo.

examples.why: It divides with nothing left over.
A factor is never larger than its number.

vocabulary.cloze: A number that divides another exactly, with no remainder, is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: The result of multiplying a number by 1, 2, 3, and so on — where you land when you skip-count by it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El resultado de multiplicar un número por 1, 2, 3, y así sucesivamente: donde caes al contar de esa cantidad.
vocabulary.cloze: What you land on counting by a number are its ___.

vocabulary.definition: The largest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. It answers “how many equal groups can I make?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más grande que es factor de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuántos grupos iguales puedo formar?”
vocabulary.cloze: The largest number that divides both is their ___ ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. It answers “when will these line up again?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más pequeño que es múltiplo de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuándo volverán a coincidir?”
vocabulary.cloze: The smallest number both numbers reach is their ___ ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two factors that multiply to make a number. In a word problem, one is the number of groups and the other is the size of each group.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos factores que se multiplican para formar un número. En un problema, uno es la cantidad de grupos y el otro el tamaño de cada grupo.
vocabulary.cloze: Two factors that multiply to make the number are a ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers, usually with a factor tree. Multiplying the primes two numbers share also gives the GCF.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como producto de números primos, normalmente con un árbol de factores. Multiplicar los primos que dos números comparten también da el MCD.
vocabulary.cloze: Writing a number as ___ numbers multiplied together is its prime factorization.

examples.why: 6 is composite; the tree is unfinished.

vocabulary.definition: A factor that two numbers both have.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor que dos números tienen en común.
vocabulary.visual: 4 is a factor of 16 and of 24.
vocabulary.cloze: A factor that two numbers share is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: The largest factor two numbers share.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mayor factor que dos números tienen en común.
vocabulary.cloze: The largest factor two numbers share is the ___.

examples.why: 8 divides both, and no larger number does.
4 is a common factor, but 8 is larger.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest multiple two numbers share.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El menor múltiplo que dos números tienen en común.
vocabulary.cloze: The smallest multiple two numbers share is the ___.

examples.why: It is the smallest number in both lists of multiples.
36 is a common multiple, but 18 is smaller.

copyPanel.rule: Greatest Common Factor (GCF) & Least Common Multiple (LCM)
steps: 1. GCF: Largest factor shared by two numbers — used to simplify fractions or divide into equal groups
2. LCM: Smallest shared multiple — used to find common denominators
3. Use prime factor trees or list method to find common factors/multiples

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Party Plans
revealWordProblem.text: Reginald is having hot dogs at his party, and 24 people are coming. His mom wants the same number of hot dogs and buns, with none left over. Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns come in packs of 8. How many packs of each should they buy, and how many hot dogs and buns will they have?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pack of hot dogs labeled 10 count beside a pack of hot dog buns labeled 8 count.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: To buy matching numbers with no unmatched hot dogs or buns, find a common multiple of the pack sizes. Multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30, 40, …; multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, …. The least common multiple is 40, so buy 4 packs of hot dogs and 5 packs of buns for 40 matched servings. This supplies at least one serving for each of 24 guests. If each guest eats exactly one, 40 − 24 = 16 matched servings remain. Thus 'none left over' can mean no unmatched hot dogs or buns; exactly 24 servings with no leftovers is impossible using only these whole packs.

questions.stem: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
questions.explanation: A factor divides 12 evenly. Every one of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12 does, and nothing else does.
choiceFeedback: 1 and 12 are factors, but so are 2, 3, 4, and 6.
This list forgets 1 and 12, which are always factors of 12.
Those are MULTIPLES of 12 — where you land skip-counting, not what divides it.
hints: Ask: what divides 12 with nothing left over?
Try each number from 1 up to 12.
Do not forget 1 and the number itself.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál lista muestra todos los factores de 12?
questions.explanationEs: Un factor divide a 12 exactamente. Cada uno de 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 y 12 lo hace, y ningún otro.
hintsEs: Pregunta: ¿qué divide a 12 sin que sobre nada?
Prueba cada número del 1 al 12.
No olvides el 1 y el número mismo.

questions.stem: Which list shows the first four multiples of 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples come from multiplying by 1, 2, 3, 4: 8, 16, 24, and 32 — the numbers you say skip-counting by 8.
choiceFeedback: Those are the FACTORS of 8 — what divides it, not what it makes.
That counts up by 1, not by 8.
hints: Skip-count by 8 out loud.
Multiples get bigger; factors stay at or below the number.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál lista muestra los primeros cuatro múltiplos de 8?
questions.explanationEs: Los múltiplos salen de multiplicar por 1, 2, 3, 4: 8, 16, 24 y 32 — los números que dices al contar de 8 en 8.
hintsEs: Cuenta de 8 en 8 en voz alta.
Los múltiplos crecen; los factores se quedan en el número o por debajo.

questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. They share 1, 2, 3, and 6 — the greatest is 6.
choiceFeedback: 2 is a common factor, but not the greatest one.
3 is a common factor, but 6 is also common and larger.
36 is a common MULTIPLE, not a factor — a factor cannot be bigger than the numbers.
hints: List the factors of each number.
Circle the numbers that appear in both lists.
Pick the largest circled number.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el máximo común divisor de 12 y 18?
questions.explanationEs: Factores de 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factores de 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Comparten 1, 2, 3 y 6 — el mayor es 6.
hintsEs: Enumera los factores de cada número.
Encierra los números que aparecen en ambas listas.
Escoge el mayor de los números encerrados.

reviewHighlights.rule: Greatest Common Factor (GCF) & Least Common Multiple (LCM)
steps: 1. GCF: Largest factor shared by two numbers — used to simplify fractions or divide into equal groups
2. LCM: Smallest shared multiple — used to find common denominators
3. Use prime factor trees or list method to find common factors/multiples
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake is reaching for the wrong tool: listing FACTORS for a problem about repeating cycles. Ayasha's classes repeat every 6 and 8 weeks, so the weeks they land on are multiples — answering with the GCF of 2 claims a class that meets every 8 weeks happens in week 2. Use the size of the answer as a check: a GCF is never larger than the smaller number, and an LCM is never smaller than the larger one.

hints: List the factors of 15 and of 25.
hintsEs: Haz una lista de los factores de 15 y de 25.
level1.explanation: List the factors of each number: 15: 1, 3, 5, 15; 25: 1, 5, 25 Choose the greatest one in both lists: GCF = 5
level1.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los factores de cada número: 15: 1, 3, 5, 15; 25: 1, 5, 25 Elige el mayor que está en las dos listas: MCD = 5

hints: Skip-count by 3 and by 4. Find the first number in both lists.
hintsEs: Cuenta de 3 en 3 y de 4 en 4. Halla el primer número que está en las dos listas.
level1.explanation: List the multiples of each number: 3: 3, 6, 9, 12; 4: 4, 8, 12 Find the least number in both lists: LCM = 12
level1.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de cada número: 3: 3, 6, 9, 12; 4: 4, 8, 12 Halla el menor número que está en las dos listas: mcm = 12

hints: List the factors of 14 and of 21. Find the greatest number in both lists.
hintsEs: Haz una lista de los factores de 14 y de 21. Halla el mayor número que está en las dos listas.
level1.explanation: List the factors of each number: 14: 1, 2, 7, 14; 21: 1, 3, 7, 21 Choose the greatest one in both lists: GCF = 7
level1.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los factores de cada número: 14: 1, 2, 7, 14; 21: 1, 3, 7, 21 Elige el mayor que está en las dos listas: MCD = 7

hints: List the factors of each number. Find the greatest number in both lists.
hintsEs: Haz una lista de los factores de cada número. Halla el mayor número que está en las dos listas.
level1.explanation: List the factors of each number: 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30 Circle the factors in both lists: 1, 2, 3, 6 Choose the greatest one: GCF = 6
level1.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los factores de cada número: 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30 Encierra los factores que están en las dos listas: 1, 2, 3, 6 Elige el mayor: MCD = 6

hints: Skip-count by 6 and by 9. Find the first number in both lists.
hintsEs: Cuenta de 6 en 6 y de 9 en 9. Halla el primer número que está en las dos listas.
level1.explanation: List the multiples of each number: 6: 6, 12, 18, 24; 9: 9, 18, 27 Find the least number in both lists: LCM = 18
level1.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de cada número: 6: 6, 12, 18, 24; 9: 9, 18, 27 Halla el menor número que está en las dos listas: mcm = 18

level2.stem: Buses leave every 15 minutes. Trains leave every 20 minutes. Both leave now. Which tells you when both leave together again?
level2.stemEs: Los autobuses salen cada 15 minutos. Los trenes salen cada 20 minutos. Los dos salen ahora. ¿Qué te dice cuándo vuelven a salir juntos?
hints: Repeating times land on multiples. Do you need a factor or a multiple?
hintsEs: Los tiempos que se repiten caen en múltiplos. ¿Necesitas un factor o un múltiplo?
level2.explanation: Decide: GCF or LCM?: repeat → multiples → LCM List the multiples: 15, 30, 45, 60; 20, 40, 60
level2.explanationEs: Decide: ¿MCD o mcm?: se repite → múltiplos → mcm Haz una lista de los múltiplos: 15, 30, 45, 60; 20, 40, 60
choiceFeedback: The GCF splits amounts into equal groups. Times that repeat need a multiple.
35 is not a multiple of 15 or of 20.

hints: Skip-count by 12. Stop at the first number that 9 also divides.
hintsEs: Cuenta de 12 en 12. Detente en el primer número que 9 también divide.
level2.explanation: List the multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36 Find the first one that 9 divides: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 → LCM = 36
level2.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 12: 12, 24, 36 Halla el primero que 9 divide: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 → mcm = 36

hints: List the factors of 20 and of 45. Find the greatest number in both lists.
hintsEs: Haz una lista de los factores de 20 y de 45. Halla el mayor número que está en las dos listas.
level2.explanation: List the factors of each number: 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20; 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45 Choose the greatest common factor: GCF = 5
level2.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los factores de cada número: 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20; 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45 Elige el máximo común divisor: MCD = 5

level2.stem: The GCF of 18 and a number n is 9. The number n is between 20 and 30. What is n?
level2.stemEs: El MCD de 18 y un número n es 9. El número n está entre 20 y 30. ¿Cuál es n?
hints: 9 must be a factor of n. Which multiples of 9 are between 20 and 30?
hintsEs: 9 debe ser un factor de n. ¿Qué múltiplos de 9 están entre 20 y 30?
level2.explanation: List multiples of 9 between 20 and 30: 27 Check the GCF of 18 and 27: 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18; 27: 1, 3, 9, 27 Name the greatest shared factor: GCF = 9
level2.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 9 entre 20 y 30: 27 Comprueba el MCD de 18 y 27: 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18; 27: 1, 3, 9, 27 Nombra el mayor factor compartido: MCD = 9

level2.stem: Napkins come in packs of 6. Plates come in packs of 15. You want the same number of napkins and plates. What is the least number of each you can buy?
level2.stemEs: Las servilletas vienen en paquetes de 6. Los platos vienen en paquetes de 15. Quieres el mismo número de servilletas y de platos. ¿Cuál es el menor número de cada uno que puedes comprar?
hints: Whole packs make multiples. Find the LCM of 6 and 15.
hintsEs: Los paquetes completos dan múltiplos. Halla el mcm de 6 y 15.
level2.explanation: List the multiples of each number: 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30; 15: 15, 30 Find the least common multiple: LCM = 30 Find the packs of each: 30 ÷ 6 = 5; 30 ÷ 15 = 2
level2.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de cada número: 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30; 15: 15, 30 Halla el mínimo común múltiplo: mcm = 30 Halla los paquetes de cada uno: 30 ÷ 6 = 5; 30 ÷ 15 = 2

level3.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 18 and 24?
choiceFeedback: 2 does divide both, but it is not the greatest one. Keep checking upward and 6 divides both too.
3 does divide both, but it is not the greatest one. 6 divides 18 and 24 as well.
That is a common MULTIPLE, and it is larger than both numbers. A factor divides into them.
level3.explanation: The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, and 18. The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24. The shared factors are 1, 2, 3, and 6, and the largest is 6.

level3.stem: Raj says the LCM of 6 and 10 is 60 because 6 × 10 = 60. What is the LCM of 6 and 10?
level3.stemEs: Raj dice que el mcm de 6 y 10 es 60 porque 6 × 10 = 60. ¿Cuál es el mcm de 6 y 10?
hints: List the multiples of 10. Which one does 6 divide first?
hintsEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 10. ¿Cuál divide 6 primero?
level3.explanation: List the multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 Find the first one that 6 divides: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 → LCM = 30
level3.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 Halla el primero que 6 divide: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 → mcm = 30

hints: Skip-count by 14. Stop at the first number that 8 also divides.
hintsEs: Cuenta de 14 en 14. Detente en el primer número que 8 también divide.
level3.explanation: List the multiples of 14: 14, 28, 42, 56 Find the first one that 8 divides: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 → LCM = 56
level3.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 14: 14, 28, 42, 56 Halla el primero que 8 divide: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 → mcm = 56

level3.stem: A florist has 45 roses and 60 daisies. She makes identical bunches with no flowers left over. What is the greatest number of bunches?
level3.stemEs: Una florista tiene 45 rosas y 60 margaritas. Hace ramos idénticos sin que sobren flores. ¿Cuál es el mayor número de ramos?
hints: Equal bunches with nothing left means a common factor. Find the greatest one.
hintsEs: Ramos iguales sin que sobre nada significa un factor común. Halla el mayor.
level3.explanation: Write each number as a product of primes: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5; 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 Multiply the shared primes: 3 × 5 = 15
level3.explanationEs: Escribe cada número como producto de primos: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5; 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 Multiplica los primos compartidos: 3 × 5 = 15

level3.stem: Two numbers have a GCF of 4 and an LCM of 24. One number is 8. What is the other number?
level3.stemEs: Dos números tienen un MCD de 4 y un mcm de 24. Uno de los números es 8. ¿Cuál es el otro número?
hints: The other number is a multiple of 4 and a factor of 24. Test each one.
hintsEs: El otro número es múltiplo de 4 y factor de 24. Prueba cada uno.
level3.explanation: List multiples of 4 that divide 24: 4, 8, 12, 24 Test 12 with 8: GCF of 8 and 12 = 4; LCM of 8 and 12 = 24 Rule out the others: 4 → GCF 4, LCM 8; 8 → GCF 8; 24 → GCF 8
level3.explanationEs: Haz una lista de los múltiplos de 4 que dividen a 24: 4, 8, 12, 24 Prueba 12 con 8: MCD de 8 y 12 = 4; mcm de 8 y 12 = 24 Descarta los demás: 4 → MCD 4, mcm 8; 8 → MCD 8; 24 → MCD 8
